segments.title: Chương 80: 0080 [Đếm ngược thi Đại học]
segments.content:
In April, the second mock exam was held.

Wails of anguish were heard everywhere!

The three mock exams each had a different focus.

The first mock exam was relatively difficult. It presented the knowledge points from all three years of high school in a comprehensive way.

The second mock exam was extremely difficult. It designed questions by linking the knowledge points from all three years of high school more closely, requiring students to be flexible and skilled in their application.

The third mock exam was easy. The college entrance exam was approaching, so it was meant to give the students a bit of confidence.

Walking out of the exam hall, Bian Guanyue felt like she was sleepwalking. She thought she had completely bombed this one.

Soon, she regained some confidence.

Because a few classmates nearby were also complaining, "Those big questions in the liberal arts comprehensive exam, and the English reading comprehension were so hard!"

"I'm afraid I won't make the Tier 1 cutoff this time."

"Me too, probably."

"Who the fuck made these questions? What a joke!"

"..."

Chen Guiliang walked out from the next exam room. Bian Guanyue hurried over, "How did you do?"

"Not bad," Chen Guiliang thought for a moment, "English was a bit of a disaster. The listening and reading comprehension were really hard to guess this time."

Bian Guanyue said, "My English was okay. During the winter break, I memorized 25 new words every day and listened to English songs while I slept every night. But my math and liberal arts comprehensive exams went terribly. A few of the big questions just left me dumbfounded."

Xie Yang also came out of the exam hall, not looking too pleased.

Chen Guiliang looked over at Xu Haibo, who was walking towards them. The well-behaved student was already on the verge of tears.

"What's wrong?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Xu Haibo wiped his tears, "Nothing, I just didn't review well enough."

Li Jun and Guan Zhiqiang were the happiest of the bunch.

Li Jun even turned in his paper early, grabbed a ball, and headed straight for the basketball court.

Guan Zhiqiang at least waited until the last minute to turn in his paper, then happily rushed towards the book rental shop.

"Let's go. We'll get some stir-fry. My treat today." Chen Guiliang felt it was time to console everyone a bit.

He called his friends, and all the brothers from dorm 302 came, and even two from 301 joined the fun.

Bian Guanyue was also invited, but she was still a bit reserved.

Especially when Xu Haibo let it slip and accidentally called her "sister-in-law," which made Bian Guanyue's pretty face flush crimson.

But after the meal was over, as Bian Guanyue was taking the bus home, she leaned against the window and smiled the whole way.

The phone rang. It was her older cousin.

"Hey, Guan Guan, you have the college entrance exam in two months, right?" her cousin asked.

Bian Guanyue said, "Yeah, I just finished the second mock exam."

"Mm... Your dad is really worried about you, but he doesn't dare to call, afraid he'll accidentally make you angry again. If you have any difficulties at school, or any worries, you can call and tell me."

"It's okay, I'm doing fine."

"How about coming to Hangcheng for university? I'll look out for you."

"I want to apply to a university in the capital."

"Why?"

"I just want to."

"Alright, if you need anything, you must call me."

The two sisters chatted for a while, and Bian Guanyue hung up as she got off the bus.

This cousin was her aunt's daughter and had always taken great care of her since they were children.

Two days later, the results of the second mock exam were out.

Compared to his first mock exam score, Chen Guiliang's hadn't changed much, only dropping by 5 points.

That's right, his score had actually dropped.

Because the exam was too difficult.

Chinese 137, Math 93, English 95, Liberal Arts Comprehensive 238. Total score 563.

However, the Tier 1 cutoff was set at 521.

Chen Guiliang surpassed the Tier 1 cutoff by a full 42 points!

The head teacher, Liu Shuying, worried that the students would be too discouraged, so she held a special class meeting to review the second mock exam. She patiently explained the differences between the first mock exam, the second mock exam, and the college entrance exam, telling the students who did poorly this time not to lose heart.

Liu Shuying also said, "Chen Guiliang's performance this time was very surprising. We won't even talk about Chinese. His liberal arts comprehensive score was the highest in the entire grade! Chen Guiliang, why don't you come up and share your experience in studying liberal arts."

What experience could he have?

Was he supposed to talk about how he frequently engaged in online political commentary, arguing heatedly with people, and looking up information whenever he couldn't win an argument?

After being reborn, he filled in the forgotten details of politics, history, and geography. With his rich knowledge from online debates, he analyzed the major questions with an adult's mindset and provided answers from the perspective of the exam setter. How could he not get a high score?

The liberal arts comprehensive scores were generally poor this time precisely because a few of the comprehensive questions were devilishly hard. Even the top student, Wu Meng, only scored 233.

Chen Guiliang, however, was completely unaffected, scoring 238 and ranking first in the school for the liberal arts comprehensive exam.

Chen Guiliang stood up and spoke correct but empty words, "For Chinese, politics, history, and geography, you still need to accumulate knowledge over time. It's just like English. I didn't study English much before, and now if I want to catch up, I can only memorize vocabulary slowly."

Liu Shuying smiled, "You did well in English this time too. Although it dropped by two points compared to the first mock exam, that's because of the difficulty of the questions. The same goes for your math score. Your math teacher told me that with a normal level of difficulty, you would definitely have scored over 100 this time. Although it's not very high, you're improving with every exam."

Chen Guiliang sat down.

Liu Shuying continued, "Everyone should learn from Chen Guiliang, especially the students in the middle ranks. You still have a lot of potential to increase your scores. As long as you review seriously every day, you'll see improvement in every exam. Those on track for Tier 2 universities can get into Tier 1, and those on track for Tier 1 can get into key universities..."

Wu Meng whispered to Bian Guanyue, "Great Hero Chen is so amazing. His liberal arts comprehensive score is even higher than mine this time."

"His liberal arts comprehensive is indeed very strong," Bian Guanyue replied with a smile.

She had thought she bombed the exam, but when the simulated admission cutoff line came out, she had actually surpassed the Tier 2 line by 16 points. Even better than her last attempt!

The second semester of senior year was just this boring.

Studying, eating, sleeping, taking exams, checking scores... an endless loop.

The only few bright spots were hearing on the school broadcast that some star had released a new song, like F.I.R.'s "Lydia" or "Our Love."

For some students, days like these felt like years.

Chen Guiliang, however, felt it was alright. He didn't think about anything all day, just studied seriously.

The extracurricular books that had occupied his time in high school in his previous life no longer interested him. The messy thoughts he had as a high school senior in his past life were now impossible to think about.

What else was there to do?

Besides studying, there didn't seem to be much to do.

If he had a smartphone, it might have distracted him.

Occasionally, after the evening self-study session, he would take a walk with Bian Guanyue. Or Tao Xue would come over, and he would tell Auntie Xue a few jokes.

In the blink of an eye, another month passed!

The third mock exam arrived.

This time, the questions were so easy that even the slackers were all smiles.

Chen Guiliang achieved an even more dazzling result: Chinese 142, Math 117, English 112, Liberal Arts Comprehensive 249. Total score 620!

However, the admission cutoff was also set high. Chen Guiliang was only 53 points above the Tier 1 line.

Bian Guanyue also reached the mid-range of Tier 2. If she got lucky during the college entrance exam, it seemed possible she might just touch the edge of the Tier 1 line.

The 100-day countdown to the college entrance exam gradually went from double digits to single digits.

10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5...

A four-day break.

"Anyone going home?" Xie Yang asked.

No one in the dorm answered.

Xie Yang asked again, "Who's not going home?"

"I'm not going back."

"Too lazy to take the bus."

"..."

No one was going back.

Xie Yang was already restless, "The college entrance exam is in four days. Reviewing more won't make much difference. How about we go to the internet cafe and play some games?"

"Forget it, I'm just going to sleep," said Li Yulin, "I haven't slept well lately. I'll take this chance to catch up."

"Sleep for all four days?"

"We'll see tomorrow. The sun's too strong today."

No one wanted to move. Xie Yang also lost the urge to go to the internet cafe. The entire dorm lay in their beds and slept for a day.

The next day was overcast, hot, and humid.

Chen Guiliang did a set of math problems, then couldn't be bothered to touch the stuff again. By afternoon, he couldn't stand it anymore and said, "Let's go. My treat. We'll go drink tea on Binjiang Road."

Great Hero Chen's appeal was clearly stronger than Xie Yang's.

One call and seven answered. Everyone was on board.

He felt it would be boring with just guys, so he called Bian Guanyue, Qin Shanshan, and Wang Siyu to come along.

Li Yulin brought his girlfriend, Wang Yu.

When everyone finally met up, the top student Wu Meng had even shown up uninvited.

Tao Xue couldn't make it; she had gone home.

At this time, Binjiang Road was lined with small-leaved banyan trees, and teahouses had set up tables directly under the trees.

Some people came just to cool off and drink tea, while others played mahjong or Fight the Landlord.

All over Sichuan and Shu, there were teahouses and tea pavilions everywhere.

Many parents who didn't have time to look after their children just left them with their grandparents. And so, the children spent their childhoods in teahouses with their grandparents.

The first characters they learned might have been one to nine and Wàn, Fā, Zhōng.

The first letters they learned might have been J, Q, K, A.

Later, the teahouses (card rooms) in residential communities became so competitive, what with the owners helping to pick up kids from school so the customers could continue playing cards without interruption. The owners were also responsible for helping to buy groceries, and even acted as part--time chefs, providing lunch free of charge...

"Boss, tea," Chen Guiliang called out.

By the Tuo River, the water flowed over the stone steps.

On top of the stone steps, in the river itself, a row of sun umbrellas and tables and chairs were set up.

A group of students took off their sandals, rolled up their pant legs, sat on the chairs, and let their feet soak in the river water.

Although the weather was hot and humid, the river breeze brought a hint of coolness.

Xie Yang was very intrigued, "How did you know about this place?"

"Yeah, it's so charming," Qin Shanshan said with excitement, "Especially drinking tea while sitting with your feet in the river. The boss who came up with this idea is a genius."

Wang Siyu laughed, "And to think you grew up in the county town. I've been to this place long ago."

Bian Guanyue leaned back in her chair, closed her eyes to feel the river breeze, and gently stirred the water with her feet, feeling an indescribable sense of ease.

This place was truly relaxing.

As for the sound of mahjong being played nearby, the people of Sichuan and Shu had long grown used to it.

"Want to play mahjong?" the owner asked as he brought the tea over.

Liu Zhihong raised his hand, "I want to play!"

Chen Guiliang said, "Playing mahjong is fine, but no gambling. The college entrance exam is just around the corner, don't get upset over losing money. If you do poorly on the exam then, you'll blame me for treating you today."

"Alright, alright, no gambling. The loser gets a piece of paper stuck on their face. Anyone have paper?"

"I have tissues."

Chen Guiliang didn't join the mahjong game. He soaked his feet in the river, felt the breeze, and stared at the distant river view, letting his mind go blank.

After transmigrating, the college entrance exam was finally here.
